Priya / team —

Quick legal read and recommendations: 

1) Withholding / credit notes — we should keep invoicing gross. If Stratify withholds amounts, we can accept a credit note only where local law requires withholding (i.e., government tax obligation). We do NOT accept unilateral withholding for commercial reasons. Add clause: "If Buyer is required by law to withhold taxes from payments, Buyer shall provide Redwood with official tax documentation and the gross-up equivalent will be resolved via a mutually agreed credit note applied at the next true-up period." I'll draft a short paragraph and attach as "legal_clause_annotations.pdf".

2) Split invoicing across entities — operationally possible but requires: (a) signed PO(s) per invoiced entity, (b) currency and VAT ID for each entity, (c) explicit mapping in Appendix A stating which band/commit applies to which entity. Finance will also need Ledgerly's remit details if they will act as a billing agent.

3) Net terms move to Net 60 — acceptable for this account subject to: signed PO on file, Ledgerly or Stratify credit check passed, and a one-time activation invoice paid up-front (we can keep the activation fee as a prepay). Marissa, if you confirm the credit check path we'll mirror this in Appendix A and update the billing milestone table.

4) Redlines: I reviewed STRAT_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx and tracked minor clarifying edits (payment sequencing and tax evidence window). I recommend sending back a marked PDF to Stratify with the proposed withholding clause and a checklist of required evidence.

I'll attach the short clause and the annotated PDF. If you want a quick call with Stratify this week I can join 30 mins.

-Kim
